title: Ethiopian Spiced Lamb Shoulder
community: Ethiopian special occasions — whole lamb shoulder preparation
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Whole Lamb Shoulder — marinated overnight in berbere, kibbeh, garlic, and ginger, slow-roasted for 2 hours until falling tender. The celebration centrepiece — carved at the table on injera and eaten communally.
longDesc: The whole lamb shoulder roast is the Ethiopian celebration showpiece — marinated overnight in berbere and kibbeh, roasted until falling-off-the-bone tender, and brought whole to the table where guests tear pieces directly. It represents the pinnacle of Ethiopian hospitality.
steps: Pierce shoulder deeply all over. Rub marinade in thoroughly. Refrigerate overnight.
Bring to room temperature 1.5 hours before roasting.
Roast covered with foil at 150°C for 90 minutes.
Remove foil. Raise to 200°C for 20—30 minutes to caramelise.
Rest 20 minutes. Pull apart or carve.
chefTips: The overnight marinade penetrates deeply through the score marks.
Low and slow for 90 minutes creates falling-tender meat.
The high-heat finish caramelises the berbere coating magnificently.
cookingScience: See ETH036 for roast science. Lamb shoulder has more connective tissue than leg — requiring the longer cooking time to convert collagen to gelatin, producing the falling-tender result.
sustainabilityTips: Shoulder is a secondary cut — more sustainable use of the whole animal.
culturalNote: The whole lamb shoulder arriving at the table is the ultimate Ethiopian hospitality statement — 'for you, we have spared nothing'.
